brief: Captures text messages instead of sending them, validates the number, and counts the billable segments a carrier would charge.
detail: A capture sink with the shape of stzMailSandbox, whose point is the bill. SMS is charged per segment, and the segment count depends on the alphabet: text within the GSM 7-bit alphabet takes 160 characters in one segment and 153 per part, and one character outside it, such as an Arabic letter or an emoji, makes the whole message UCS-2 with 70 and 67; nine characters of the extension table cost two septets each. Send names the encoding and the segments, and TotalSegments lets a test assert the cost. Numbers must be E.164. An outage is refused and recorded nowhere, while a bad number is rejected, so retrying and fixing the data are told apart. The honest limit: a sink shows what you would have sent, not that a carrier would accept it. The outbox is shared by copies of the object.
